absent_by_design: merge tool / merge endpoint (human gate — see human_merge_gate)
delete tools / delete endpoints (exposure is a safety decision, same as TicketDesk)

app.database: targets/engineering/engineering.db (own SQLite file, like every target)

ci_rule.implemented_in: targets/engineering/seed.py: compute_ci (single source of truth — app.py calls it at PR creation, seed.py calls it for the pre-seeded PRs)
ci_rule.statement: A PR passes CI iff (a) every keyword in the issue's acceptance_keywords appears in the PR's change_summary (case-insensitive), AND (b) the PR's files_touched is a superset of the issue's files list.
ci_rule.timing: evaluated once, when the PR is opened; the stored ci_results row never changes afterwards

human_merge_gate: PLATFORM RULE: agents prepare PRs, humans merge them. This workplace has NO merge endpoint and NO merge tool, and no delete endpoints/tools at all. A PR record's terminal state inside the system is 'approved' (reachable only with green CI and a reviewer who is not the author). Merging — and closing the issue as done — is a human action taken outside the tool surface.

templates.check: checks.check_work_issue (newest worker PR on the issue)

mirrors: targets/ticketdesk — same layout: app.py (FastAPI system of record), seed.py, reset.py, mcp_server.py (generated-style Synapse Auto server), README.md, requirements.txt

reset.cli: python3 reset.py (deletes engineering.db and reseeds — identical semantics to TicketDesk/StockRoom)
reset.http: POST /admin/reset (internal route, NOT in the tool allowlist)
reset.restores: 12 issues, 3 PRs (open / changes_requested / approved), 3 CI rows (pass / fail / pass), 3 notes

state.ci_results: one immutable CI row per PR, computed by the service's deterministic CI rule at PR creation
state.issues: ~12 seeded engineering issues with labels + priority (4 deliberately unlabelled/unprioritised for the triage job); each solvable issue carries an acceptance statement, acceptance keywords and a required file list
state.notes: engineering notes on issues, optionally tied to a PR
state.pull_requests: PR records linked to issues, in states open / changes_requested / approved (3 seeded, one in each state)

synapse_onboarding.direct_mode: FLOOR_MCP_MODE=direct equivalent is exercised by targets/engineering/verify_e2e.py, whose DirectClient implements the identical tool mapping over plain httpx (the same fallback contract as mcp_manager/orchestrator.tools). Registering server_kind 'engineering' in mcp_manager/client.py + orchestrator/tools.py TOOL_SPECS (base URL env ENGINEERING_URL, default http://localhost:8106) is the one remaining integration step, left to the integrator — this build does not modify those shared files.
synapse_onboarding.flow_per_docs: cd targets/engineering && synapse build --local --auto --all-endpoints (Auto allowlist = the endpoints behind the tools above), producing synapse_auto_server.py — the same flow that produced TicketDesk's server
synapse_onboarding.status: PENDING — with reason: the synapse CLI is not installed on this VM (`synapse: command not found`; an npx fetch of @2ndbrainlabs-ai/synapse-cli did not complete in this environment), and a --local build additionally needs the Groq key staged per docs/SYNAPSE_NOTES.md §3. Exactly as with TicketDesk and StockRoom, targets/engineering/mcp_server.py is the generated-style stand-in: same tool names, same allowlist, same read/write prefixes, thin HTTP passthroughs — swapping in a real synapse_auto_server.py changes no contract.

tools.note: Names/effects mirror targets/*/mcp_server.py: read_/write_ prefix = effect. Every write is confirm-gated by the factory before dispatch (ARCHITECTURE §4.3). Tool layer file: targets/engineering/mcp_server.py (stdio MCP, thin HTTP passthroughs to the app).

write.name: write_triage_issue
write.note: labels + priority assignment; required by the triage job template

write.name: write_open_pr
write.note: requires the issue to be claimed by the PR author; runs CI immediately

write.name: write_request_changes
write.note: reviewer-side; reviewer must not be the PR author

write.name: write_approve_pr
write.note: reviewer-side; requires recorded CI = pass; approval is NOT a merge

verification.covers: service boot on :8106, every tool exercised (direct mode + one MCP stdio list/call), negative CI case, reviewer gates (self-review rejected, red-CI approve rejected), and job template work_issue run end-to-end with checks.check_work_issue passing
